gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured on-water speed. Cruising World timed the Torqeedo Travel 1103 S at 4.3 kn and the ePropulsion Spirit 1.0 Evo at 4.2 kn on the same 8 ft inflatable, and a 2.5 hp Mercury gas outboard reached only 4.6 kn on that boat.
standout_why: I compared the two cited pages, epropulsion.com eLite and torqeedo.com Travel M-1160-00, plus the top results sparkpowered.com and the Yacht & Ocean guide (which returns a 404). The ePropulsion and Torqeedo pages give only the maker's own runtime and speed tables: eLite 4.7 mph and 45 min at 500 W, Travel S 8.6 km/h and 0:47 at full throttle, neither with a named tester. Sparkpowered says its ranges are 'the makers' own claims in calm water' and cites no magazine test. None of these pages has a GPS speed, a bollard pull or a runtime measured by a named tester. One caveat: the measured units are earlier or sister models (Travel 1103, Spirit 1.0 Evo/Plus). I found no measurement of the current Travel S, eLite (by a magazine) or kLite 750.
decides: The tests confirm the page's split rather than reverse it. A 1 kW motor with a clip-on battery (Spirit 1.0 Plus, which ePropulsion says floats) tops out at about 4 kn on a dinghy in two independent tests, Cruising World and Yachting Monthly. That is close to a 2.5 hp gas outboard. The 500 W eLite with its battery built in measured about 4 kn too, but only for about 45 min. For a kayak, Boating Magazine ran the Newport NK180 with Newport's 24 V 50 Ah battery for more than 8 miles over 4 hours in saltwater on less than half a charge. That backs the NK180 bundle as the all-day fishing pick, while the 378 Wh built-in units suit short tender runs.

findings.label: Top speed and runtime at full power (Cruising World)
findings.source_title: Gear Test: Electric Motors for Dinghy Engines (Mark Pillsbury, Cruising World, 2023-06-30)
findings.note: 8 ft West Marine inflatable, about 5 kn of wind and small waves. At half throttle (about 500 W): 3.3 kn SOG and about 2 h 20 min. At about 100 W: 2.3 kn with an estimated 9 h. The low-battery beep came with 10 min left. The Evo is the Spirit 1.0 Plus plus regeneration.

findings.label: Top speed and range wide open (Cruising World)
findings.source_title: Gear Test: Electric Motors for Dinghy Engines (Mark Pillsbury, Cruising World, 2023-06-30)
findings.note: Same 8 ft inflatable. At 500 W: 3.6 kn and about 1.5 h (battery not full at the start). At 20 W: 1.1 kn and 37 h. This is the predecessor of the current Travel S that ChatGPT showed.

findings.label: Gas reference on the same boat (Cruising World)
findings.source_title: Gear Test: Electric Motors for Dinghy Engines (Mark Pillsbury, Cruising World, 2023-06-30)
findings.note: Measured with a navigation app. That is 0.3 to 0.4 kn faster than the 1 kW electrics.

findings.label: Top speed at maximum output (Yachting Monthly)
findings.source_title: Best electric outboard motor: We put the market leaders to the test (Theo Stocker, Yachting Monthly, 2026-11-11)
findings.note: Average speed from a handheld GPS, runs in both directions, main test boat a Boatworld Air V 250. YM writes that the 'over an hour at full speed' runtime is theoretical. Listed weights: 10.9 kg motor with bracket, 8.6 kg battery, 1,276 Wh.

findings.source_title: Best electric outboard motor: We put the market leaders to the test (Theo Stocker, Yachting Monthly, 2026-11-11)

findings.source_title: MotorsTest - Electric outboard comparison (Johannes Erdmann, BOOTE, 2020-09-27)

findings.source_title: MotorsTest - Electric outboard comparison (Johannes Erdmann, BOOTE, 2020-09-27)
findings.note: Same boats as the Spirit test. 0 to full speed in 9 s (Spirit: 9.5 s). Older model generation.

findings.label: Top speed, runtime and range at full power (PMR Sailing)
findings.value: about 4 kn; about 45 min; about 3 nm (about 1.5 h and 4.5 nm at 250 W)
findings.source_title: ePropulsion eLite review (Philip M Russell, PMR Sailing, 2024-08-02)
findings.note: RS Toura dinghy with two adults on a river. A named owner-reviewer, not a lab. Powerboat & RIB's eLite review repeats only ePropulsion's 45 min at 4 kn claim.

findings.label: Top speed and endurance with Newport 24 V 50 Ah battery (Boating Magazine)
findings.value: 5 mph at 100% on a calm lake; more than 8 miles in a 4 h saltwater run using under 50% of the battery
findings.source_title: Newport NK180 kayak motor review (Chris Woodward, Boating Magazine, 2024-04-01)
findings.note: 12 ft Hobie Mirage Compass (68 lb). Nearly 6 mph with current and wind. Nearly 1 h at 83% throttle. The writer weighed the battery at 37 lb, which fills the missing battery weight in our NK180 row. 24 V × 50 Ah = 1,280 Wh, so under 640 Wh was used for more than 8 mi. He confirmed charging takes about 4 h from 30%.
